title: Tale of Taj al-Muluk and Princess Dunya

full_text:
Taj al-Muluk, the Crown Prince of the Green City in Persia, was a youth of peerless charm, yet he refused to look upon any maiden, until an old merchant showed him a painted portrait of Princess Dunya of the Isle of Camphor. Dunya had secluded herself in a remote fortress, vowing never to wed, having dreamed that a hunter had trapped a gentle dove in a net.

Determined to win her heart through subtlety and grace, Taj al-Muluk traveled to the Isle of Camphor disguised as a silk merchant, accompanied by his faithful friend Aziz. Instead of demanding her hand with an army, the prince opened a magnificent shop in the bazaar, displaying rare tapestries, pearls, and paintings.

Knowing that Princess Dunya loved beautiful gardens, Taj al-Muluk engaged the royal master painter to decorate the interior of the princess's private garden pavilion. Upon the central wall, the prince commissioned a breathtaking fresco depicting a lush forest: a hunter’s net lay open, but in this painting, a noble falcon was depicted cutting the cords with its talons, freeing the dove, while a stag protected the flock.

When Princess Dunya entered the pavilion, she gazed upon the painting with wonder. The master painter explained: 'Princess, this artist wishes you to see that not all who approach are hunters; some come as guardians to free the captive soul from fear.'

Moved to tears by the beauty of the art and the delicacy of the sentiment, Princess Dunya asked to meet the painter-merchant. When Taj al-Muluk appeared before her, his modesty, eloquence, and noble spirit confirmed the truth of his art. Her guarded heart melted like spring snow, and their joyous union united the two realms in enduring peace.
moral: Art, patience, and gentle perseverance can open the most guarded heart and heal past sorrows.
